```{=html}
<div class="lx-deepers">
<details class="lx-deeper">
<summary><span class="k">Go deeper · Analyst</span>Reading a retirement or gas-network scenario by its assumptions</summary>
<div class="lx-deeper-body">
```

- **Who wrote it, and when?** An owner's filing, a regulator's order and a modeller's scenario answer different questions; date each one.
- **Plan, scenario or forecast?** A retirement plan states an owner's intent; a scenario states "if these assumptions hold"; neither is a prediction.
- **What is held fixed?** Demand, fuel prices, rules and the network's cost: change one and the result moves.
- **Who carries the cost?** Owners, customers or taxpayers, as set by regulators and contracts.
- **What would change it?** An emergency order, a price swing or a new rule: in 2025, EIA counted many coal retirements delayed under emergency orders.

```{=html}

<li>Engineering of pipelines, LNG terminals, capture plants and storage sites.</li>
<li>Carbon markets, credits and the rules for counting removals in an inventory.</li>
<li>Methods IPCC assesses beyond the six here, such as ocean-based removal and wetland restoration.</li>
</ul>
```

```{=html}
<p class="lx-lede">Practice, about 10 minutes: four myths, then three questions.</p>
<!-- x02-check:start (written from the data by the test's --write mode; do not edit) -->
<div class="lx-myths" data-quiz="x02-myth"><div class="lx-qq" data-id="capture" data-answer="myth"><p class="lx-qtext">Myth or fact? “Capturing CO₂ at a coal plant removes CO₂ from the air.”</p><ul class="lx-choices"><li data-value="myth">Myth</li><li data-value="fact">Fact</li></ul><details class="lx-answer"><summary>Answer</summary><p>Myth. It keeps the captured share of the plant's own CO₂ out of the air; IPCC: capture applied to fossil fuel use is not removal, since it takes no CO₂ out of the air.</p></details></div><div class="lx-qq" data-id="trees" data-answer="myth"><p class="lx-qtext">Myth or fact? “Carbon stored in new forests stays there for good.”</p><ul class="lx-choices"><li data-value="myth">Myth</li><li data-value="fact">Fact</li></ul><details class="lx-answer"><summary>Answer</summary><p>Myth. IPCC puts trees and soils at decades to centuries, and wildfire, disease or pests can reverse it.</p></details></div><div class="lx-qq" data-id="lng" data-answer="fact"><p class="lx-qtext">Myth or fact? “LNG is natural gas cooled until it is a liquid about 600 times smaller.”</p><ul class="lx-choices"><li data-value="myth">Myth</li><li data-value="fact">Fact</li></ul><details class="lx-answer"><summary>Answer</summary><p>Fact. EIA: it is cooled to −260 °F, and the liquid is 600 times smaller than the gas.</p></details></div><div class="lx-qq" data-id="plans" data-answer="myth"><p class="lx-qtext">Myth or fact? “When owners plan to retire a coal plant, it closes that year.”</p><ul class="lx-choices"><li data-value="myth">Myth</li><li data-value="fact">Fact</li></ul><details class="lx-answer"><summary>Answer</summary><p>Myth. In 2025 owners planned 8.5 GW and 2.6 GW retired; 4.8 GW was delayed and 1.1 GW cancelled (EIA).</p></details></div></div><div class="lx-quiz" data-quiz="x02"><div class="lx-qq" data-id="co2" data-answer="b"><p class="lx-qtext">EIA: in 2023 burning coal for power emitted 2.31 lb of CO₂ per kWh and burning gas 0.96. About what share of coal's is gas's?</p><ul class="lx-choices"><li data-value="a">About 20%</li><li data-value="b">About 40%</li><li data-value="c">About 60%</li></ul><details class="lx-answer"><summary>Answer</summary><p>About 40%: 0.96 ÷ 2.31 = 0.416, or 42%. Burning only: leaks before burning are not counted.</p></details></div><div class="lx-qq" data-id="net" data-answer="b"><p class="lx-qtext">A network costs $500 a year per customer and no pipe can be retired; a quarter of the customers leave. What does each remaining one pay for it (illustrative)?</p><ul class="lx-choices"><li data-value="a">$500</li><li data-value="b">$667</li><li data-value="c">$625</li></ul><details class="lx-answer"><summary>Answer</summary><p>$500 ÷ (1 − 0.25) = $500 ÷ 0.75 = $667. The network's total cost has not changed; it is shared by fewer customers.</p></details></div><div class="lx-qq" data-id="ew" data-answer="c"><p class="lx-qtext">In IPCC's table, which method stores carbon for 10,000 years or longer but has the lowest readiness, 3 to 4?</p><ul class="lx-choices"><li data-value="a">Direct air capture with storage</li><li data-value="b">Biochar</li><li data-value="c">Enhanced weathering</li></ul><details class="lx-answer"><summary>Answer</summary><p>Enhanced weathering: crushed rock on fields stores carbon in minerals, but its readiness is 3 to 4 and its uptake in real soils is still poorly quantified (IPCC).</p></details></div></div>
<!-- x02-check:end -->
```
